title: Binder Transactions, Proxies, Stubs, Identity, and Death

scout.purpose: Understand binder transactions, proxies, stubs, identity, and death as a causal Android engineering system rather than a vocabulary item.
scout.realWorldUse: Expert Android diagnosis requires tracing responsibility through processes, framework services, threads, queues, graphics buffers, and system composition.
scout.outcome: You can explain, inspect, test, and safely apply binder transactions, proxies, stubs, identity, and death.

blocks.text: Binder makes a remote call resemble a method invocation, but proxy code serializes arguments into a Parcel and submits a transaction to the Binder driver. The driver routes it to a target process and thread; a stub unmarshals data, enforces the interface, invokes implementation code, and returns a reply for synchronous calls. Objects and file descriptors can be passed as Binder references or handles rather than copied as ordinary data. Transaction buffers are bounded, so Binder is for commands and structured metadata, not large payload transport.

blocks.text: Synchronous calls block the caller until reply; one-way calls return after queueing but are ordered per Binder node and can still apply backpressure. The callee can inspect the kernel-provided calling UID or PID, but nested work may clear or restore identity deliberately. Authorization must occur before clearing identity and must not trust caller-supplied package names. RemoteException and DeadObjectException reflect process boundaries. A death recipient observes endpoint death but does not make an interrupted operation atomic or automatically safe to retry.

blocks.code: val service = IExample.Stub.asInterface(binder); try { service.update(request) } catch (dead: DeadObjectException) { reconnectWithoutBlindReplay() }
blocks.caption: A focused inspection or implementation fragment; interpret it within its process, thread, lifecycle, security, and version context.

blocks.text: Design AIDL interfaces with bounded immutable data, explicit versioning, semantic errors, cancellation, timeouts at higher layers, and idempotency where retries are possible. Never hold application locks across a Binder call: the remote side can call back, wait, die, or take an unrelated lock. Measure transaction and scheduling latency with Perfetto, inspect binder_calls_stats where permitted, and exercise service death, caller cancellation, large payload rejection, permission denial, and callback reentrancy.

Platform internals are a causal map for diagnosis, not an invitation to depend on hidden APIs. Trace ownership across process, thread, Binder, token, queue, buffer, and display boundaries; distinguish public contracts from release-specific implementation. Use AOSP source matching the device branch, Perfetto, dumpsys, logcat, bug reports, and controlled experiments as complementary evidence. Record Android build, device, configuration, process state, workload, and timestamps. Test death, cancellation, reentrancy, backpressure, configuration, multi-window, and resource pressure. When a private class or trace label changes, the explanation should still stand at the responsibility level. Production apps use supported APIs, while platform changes require compatibility tests, security policy, boot and performance evidence, and safe rollback.

blocks.title: Common systems trap
blocks.text: Watch carefully for this common failure mode in production: Holding a mutex while making a synchronous Binder call can deadlock when the remote service calls back into code that needs the same mutex.

trap_check.mistake: Holding a mutex while making a synchronous Binder call can deadlock when the remote service calls back into code that needs the same mutex.
trap_check.why: It collapses distinct ownership or timing boundaries and can produce a confident but incorrect diagnosis.
trap_check.fix: Trace the complete causal path with matching source and runtime evidence before changing the system.

trap_check.mistake: Depending on a hidden API, internal class name, trace label, or one device observation as a stable application contract.
trap_check.why: Platform implementation and vendor behavior can change while public compatibility guarantees remain different.
trap_check.fix: Use internals for explanation and diagnosis, but implement app behavior through supported APIs and test across versions.

challenge_intro.task: Design and test a versioned AIDL operation with permission checks, bounded data, cancellation, service death, callback reentrancy, idempotency, and trace evidence.
challenge_intro.successLooksLike: The result includes a correct causal model, reproducible evidence, adverse-path testing, compatibility boundaries, and an owned regression or recovery plan.

recall.prompt: Why must authorization happen before clearCallingIdentity?
recall.answer: The original kernel-supplied caller identity is the trustworthy subject; clearing it changes subsequent checks to the service identity.

recall.prompt: What must be recorded with systems evidence?
recall.answer: The Android and app build, device, configuration, starting state, workload, process or thread context, and exact capture method.

recall.prompt: How should application code use platform-internals knowledge?
recall.answer: Use it to diagnose and reason about public behavior, not to depend on hidden implementation APIs or names.
